kind: Two small fixes with one thing in common: each is a place where a derived value drifted from the fact it was supposed to track. (a) core/planning.ts acceptanceClusters reads two checks on ONE subject as two clusters, so validateQueue rejects a legitimate item and pushes the planner toward worse acceptance criteria; found while walking phase 13's correction loops (C-083). (b) adapter/continuation.ts UNIVERSAL_META_TOOLS restates four tool names core/gates-phase.ts owns, with no guard — the implementer that added it flagged the drift rather than hiding it (C-085).
authoredBy: orchestrator — (a) reproduced directly against core/planning.ts:229-243 and validateQueue; (b) read from the C-085 implementer's own judgementCalls and confirmed at continuation.ts.
bindings: Neither discharges a manifest row. (a) removes a workaround the phase-13 e2e had to adopt (a two-check criterion collapsed onto one line, flagged in a comment there) — that workaround should be revertible once this lands. (b) closes a fresh instance of this build's most-repeated defect class, two spellings of one fact.
verifiedAgainstHead: core/planning.ts:229-243 acceptanceClusters — for each criterion it splits on whitespace, takes the first token, and strips ONLY leading and trailing non-[\w./-] runs: `raw.replace(/^[^\w./-]+/, "").replace(/[^\w./-]+$/, "").toLowerCase()`. Internal punctuation is left in place.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: acceptance ['pad("a") === "[a]"', 'pad("") === ""'] yields subjects `pad("a` and `pad` — the first keeps an internal `("` because only the TRAILING `")` was stripped, the second loses `("")` entirely because it IS trailing. Same function, two clusters. validateQueue then reports: 'item "S1" is too large: its acceptance spans 2 clusters (pad("a, pad), over the one-cluster item budget — split it into one item per cluster (§3.2)' — quoting the nonsense cluster name `pad("a` back at the planner.

core/planning.ts:205-216 — the NON_SUBJECT_TOKENS comment records this function already being fixed once for the determiner case, where 'ordinary English broke the cluster count in both directions'. This is the same class one layer down: ordinary CALL SYNTAX, which §3.2's observable-check row actively asks for, breaks it.

The one-cluster rule itself is correct and is NOT in scope: §3.2's size row rejects '> 1 acceptance cluster' and the docstring's intent — 'Criteria that share a subject stay ONE cluster however many they are, so an item may pin several observable checks on the same behaviour' — is exactly what the subject scan fails to deliver.

adapter/continuation.ts UNIVERSAL_META_TOOLS — a hand-written list of four names (conductor_status, conductor_decide, conductor_surface, conductor_defer) used to decide whether the legal set contains anything position-specific. core/gates-phase.ts legalTools is the owner of that fact.

The C-085 implementer's own finding, quoted: 'I tried to derive them instead and could not: legalTools over the same run with an empty item list returns that same set (plus conductor_answer when a question is open), so no counterfactual separates "universal" from "position-specific". If gates-phase ever adds a fifth always-legal meta tool, this list must follow it by hand.' That sentence is the derivation the guard needs — an empty-item-list run with no open question is exactly the probe.
specGaps: FC-SG-1 (what a SUBJECT is). The fix must map `pad("a")`, `pad("")` and `pad` to one subject while keeping the existing behaviour that makes `config.load` a subject distinct from `config` — dots, slashes and hyphens are part of an identifier, parentheses and quotes are not. The narrow reading: after the existing determiner skip, take the token's LEADING identifier run and stop at the first character that cannot appear inside one. Anything broader risks collapsing genuinely different subjects into one cluster, which would make the size guard too permissive instead of too strict.

FC-SG-2 (the guard must not become a second list). Row (b) is closed by DERIVING the universal set from legalTools, not by writing the four names into a test — a test-side copy would be a third spelling, not a guard.
FC-SG-3 (out of scope). Neither the one-cluster budget itself nor legalTools' composition changes. This is two derivations being made faithful to the facts they already claim to track.

assertions.text: two acceptance criteria that assert about the SAME subject count as ONE cluster however they are phrased, which is what the function's own docstring already promises ('an item may pin several observable checks on the same behaviour'): the measured failing case ['pad("a") === "[a]"', 'pad("") === ""'] yields exactly one subject and validateQueue ACCEPTS the item, and the same holds for a bare-identifier phrasing of the same pair. Asserted through validateQueue, not only through acceptanceClusters, because the rejection the planner actually sees is the thing that was wrong

the size guard is not loosened into uselessness: two criteria about genuinely DIFFERENT subjects still count as two clusters and are still rejected — including the near-miss pair that must stay distinct, `config.load` versus `config`, so the fix cannot be a blanket 'strip everything after the first word'. Both directions in one test, because a fix that collapsed every criterion to one subject would satisfy the row above and destroy the guard

the determiner handling core/planning.ts:205-216 records already fixing stays fixed: a criterion opening with an article resolves to the same subject as the same criterion without one ('the parser rejects X' and 'parser preserves Y' are ONE cluster), and two criteria that differ only by article do not become two. This row exists because the previous fix to this function was to the same scan and a careless rewrite would undo it

when the guard does reject, the violation text names subjects a human recognises: no cluster name in a validateQueue violation contains an unbalanced quote or parenthesis. The measured defect quoted `pad("a` at the planner, which is not a thing that exists in the item

adapter/continuation.ts's UNIVERSAL_META_TOOLS agrees with what core/gates-phase.ts legalTools actually legalizes for a position that says nothing about where the run is — derived at run time by asking legalTools over a run with an EMPTY item list and no open question (the probe the C-085 implementer identified), never by writing the four names into the test. If gates-phase adds or renames an always-legal meta tool, this goes RED instead of the continuation engine silently misjudging which tools are position-specific
